_comment: The request-page UI's words, in one place, because they are the design.
Generated from here: Shared/RequestPage/Copy.swift (what the app shows) and
tools/contact-sheet.html (what Matt reviews). Edit this file, run
tools/gen-request-copy.py, commit all three. CI diffs the generated files,
so the sheet cannot drift from the app the way a mockup does.
Glossary rules: request, never book. Ask, accept, decline. Never reserve,

dormantRow.title: Request page
dormantRow.blurb: Let people ask you for a time. Nothing leaves this Mac until you turn it on.
dormantRow.blurbPhone: Let people ask you for a time. Nothing leaves this iPhone until you turn it on.

explainer.title: A page where people can ask for a time
paragraphs: You offer a handful of times you are willing to be asked about. Someone opens your page, picks one, and tells you who they are.
Nothing lands in your calendar until you accept. Every request comes to this device and you answer it here — askwhen.me cannot write to your calendar, because you never give it access.

Turning this on means a server holds two things: the times you chose to offer, and requests from people who asked for one. It never sees your calendar, your events, your address, or your name beyond the label you pick.
explainer.cost: Setting it up is free and happens entirely on this device. Publishing a page needs a subscription — free for the first 90 days — and that comes at the end, after you have seen the page you would be publishing.
explainer.footnote: Nothing has been sent anywhere. Setting this up does not send anything either — the first time this app touches the network is the moment you ask to see the price.

calendars.blockCaption: Events here make you unavailable, so no time that clashes with one is ever offered. Turn this on for every calendar that holds real commitments.
calendars.useCaption: Requests you accept are written here as ordinary events. Exactly one calendar.
calendars.privacy: Only the busy-or-free shape of these calendars is ever read. Titles, locations, attendees, notes and which calendar an event came from stop at this device and are never published.
calendars.noneBlocking: No calendar is blocking yet, so every hour in your day would be offered. Pick at least one.
calendars.noRequestCalendar: Pick one calendar for accepted requests to be written into.
calendars.readOnly: Read-only — accepted requests cannot be written here.

display.nameCaption: Required, and the only thing on your page that identifies you — everything else a visitor sees is a list of times. Any label works: your name, your initials, or what you do. You decide how much that discloses.
display.blurbPlaceholder: 30 minutes, usually about refereeing or calendars.
display.blurbCaption: Sits under your name. Anyone with the link reads it, so keep it to what the time is for.
display.titleCaption: What the event is called in your calendar. You choose it, never the person asking — a stranger's words do not become a title in your calendar. What they write goes in the event's notes, where it is obviously theirs.
display.locationPlaceholder: Optional — a room, or a link
display.locationCaption: Goes into the event and into the calendar file the person receives, so whoever you accept will see it.
display.nameMissing: A page needs a name. Without one it looks like a form asking a stranger for their email address, which is what a phishing page looks like too.

policy.sentence: Answer it the way you would say it out loud. The preview underneath shows real dates, so a mistake is visible before anyone else sees it.
policy.zoneCaption: Stated, not guessed from this device. A laptop that travels must not quietly re-read “my day starts at 9” as 9am somewhere else.
policy.lunchCaption: One mid-day gap. A list of arbitrary exclusions would be a second calendar wearing a disguise — put those in a blocking calendar instead.
policy.horizonCaption: How far out someone can ask. A longer horizon puts more of your future shape on one screen, so this is a privacy control as much as an accuracy one. Between 2 and 45 days; beyond that the times are fiction, because calendars fill.
policy.noticeCaption: Nothing inside this window is offered. It guards against a request landing with less warning than your device needs to collect it.
policy.maxPerDayCaption: This matters more than it looks. Publishing every free half-hour tells a stranger your week is empty; offering four says nothing about the other twelve.
policy.slotCaption: The same number becomes the meeting length on your page and in the calendar file you send.
policy.alignCaption: Offers begin on a multiple of this past the hour, so people see :00 and :30 rather than :07. Only values that divide into 60 are offered, because the others walk through the hour.
policy.bufferCaption: Held free around anything real in your calendar, so nothing lands wheel-to-wheel against a meeting the person asking cannot see.

preview.headingOne: You are offering %d time across %d days
preview.headingMany: You are offering %d times across %d days
preview.privacy: A gap on your page could be a meeting, your lunch, a day you blacked out, or simply your daily cap. Nothing on the page says which, and that is the point.

reasons.pastDayEnd: would run past the end of your day

dayReasons.weekdayNotOffered: You do not offer this weekday.
dayReasons.dayUnavailable: This device could not resolve the day.

problems.unknownTimeZone: This device does not know the zone your policy names, so nothing is offered at all. Pick the zone again.
problems.dayWindowInvalid: The start and end of your day do not make a usable window.
problems.maxPerDayNotPositive: Your daily cap is zero, so nothing can be offered.

preview.cappedNote: Times you could have offered and chose not to. That is a different answer to “why is nothing showing” than being busy.
preview.stale: Calculated just now from the calendars on this device. Nothing here has been published.
preview.emptyPage: Your page would be empty. Nobody can ask you for anything until something is offered — the reasons are on each day below.

offer.heading: Publish your page
offer.lede: Everything so far has stayed on this device. Publishing puts the times you just previewed on askwhen.me, where the people you send the link to can ask for one.
offer.network: Loading the price is the first time this app has contacted anyone. It asks Apple what a subscription costs in your currency — nothing about you, your calendar or your page is sent, and askwhen.me is still not involved.
offer.failedTitle: Could not reach the App Store
offer.failedBody: Apple did not answer, so there is no price to show. Nothing is wrong with your page — it is still here, still on this device. Try again when you have a connection.
offer.noTrialNote: Apple gives one free trial per person, and you have used yours. The price below is what it costs from today.
offer.renews: Renews yearly until you cancel. Cancel any time in Settings — during the free trial nothing is charged at all.
offer.upgradesNote: Both of these are upgrades you can take whenever you want one. Neither carries a free trial, and neither is worth buying before you have a page — a nicer address is not much use without something at it.
offer.restoredNone: Apple has no subscription on file for this Apple Account.
offer.cancelled: No problem — nothing was bought and nothing changed. Your page is still here whenever you want it.
offer.pendingBody: Apple is holding this until someone approves it — Ask to Buy, or a payment method that needs confirming. The moment it clears, your page publishes itself. You can close the app.
offer.alreadyBody: This Apple Account has an active AskWhen.me subscription, so there is nothing to buy. Publishing your page is the only step left.
offer.createFailedTitle: Apple said yes, askwhen.me did not answer
offer.createFailedBody: Your subscription went through — you have not been charged twice and you will not be. The page itself could not be created just now. Try again; nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated.
offer.tokenWarning: Your page is kept alive by a key held only on this device, in its keychain. There is no account and no password, so it cannot be emailed to you or recovered — if you lose this device, you make a new page.

live.heading: Your page is live
live.lede: Send this link to anyone you want to be able to ask you for a time. There is nothing for them to install and no account for them to make.
live.openNote: Worth looking at once, the way the people you send it to will see it.
live.tokenHeading: This device holds the only key
live.tokenBody: Your page is kept alive by a key stored in this device's keychain. There is no account and no password, so nobody — including us — can email it to you or recover it. If you lose this device you make a new page and send out a new link.
live.publisherBody: It derives the times and uploads them whenever your calendar changes. Your other devices can still collect requests and answer them; only this one publishes, so two devices can never disagree about when you are free.
live.offBody: Switching the request page off stops publishing immediately and the page goes dark. Your subscription is Apple's to cancel, in Settings.
live.notPublished: Nothing has been published yet — the first upload happens on the next sync.

notification.acceptedBody: %@ is in your calendar. They have been sent the details.
notification.declinedBody: %@ has been told, and the time is free again.
notification.conflictTitle: Could not accept — that time is taken
notification.conflictBody: Something landed on %@ since it was offered. Nothing was written. Open Calendar Mirror to see the alternatives.
notification.failedTitle: Accepted, but askwhen.me was not told
notification.failedBody: The event is in your calendar. The person who asked has not been sent it yet — open the app to finish.
notification.permissionBody: Requests arrive on your device, not in an inbox. A notification is how you find out one is waiting, and it carries Accept and Decline so you can answer without opening anything.
notification.permissionNote: Whoever asked gave their name and a note, and both appear in the notification. If you would rather they did not show on a locked screen, iOS controls that under Notifications → Show Previews.
notification.permissionDenied: Notifications are off for Calendar Mirror. Requests still arrive and still wait for you in the app — you just will not be told. Settings → Notifications turns them back on.

conflict.title: That time is taken
conflict.lede: %@ asked for %@, and something has landed on it since you offered it. Nothing has been written, and nobody has been told anything yet.
conflict.landedNote: Shown as a time only. This is the same busy/free view the page is built from — the app does not read what your events are called.
conflict.alternativesNote: Declining tells them the time is gone. There is no way to offer one of these back to them from here — they would have to ask again — so if one of these works, say so when you reply.
conflict.noAlternatives: Nothing else is open inside your horizon. Declining is the honest answer.
conflict.acceptAnywayNote: Writes it into your calendar on top of whatever is there. Sometimes that is exactly right — you know what the clash is and this matters more.
conflict.laterNote: It stays in your queue. The time is held for whoever asked until the hold runs out, and then the slot goes back on offer.
